items.title: 1.6.1 Graphical Behaviour of Logarithmic Functions (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle topic mein hum ne logarithmic function ki definition aur us ke laws dekhe. Ab sawal yeh hai ke is ka graph kaisa dikhta hai, aur kyun? Graph banane se pehle ek achha student function ki 'personality' samajhta hai: kahan defined hai, kis line ke qareeb jata hai, axes ko kahan kaat-ta hai, upar jata hai ya neeche. Is topic mein yahi chaar cheezein qadam ba qadam saabit karenge.

Kitab kehti hai: is section mein hum logarithmic function \(y = \log_a x\) (domain \(]0, \infty[\), range \(]-\infty, \infty[\)) ke graph ka rawaiya (behaviour) tarteeb se dekhenge: vertical asymptote, base \(a\) ki mukhtalif values par curve ki shakal, intercepts, continuity, injectivity, aur yeh ke function barhta hai ya ghatta hai. Yeh sab properties mil kar batati hain ke curve kaisa chalta hai, aur graph ko durust banane aur samajhne ki buniyad deti hain.
(i) Injectivity of Logarithmic Functions

Injectivity ka matlab one-to-one hona hai: do alag inputs kabhi same output na dein. Saabit karne ka tareeqa yeh hai ke hum maan lete hain ke do outputs barabar hain, aur dikhate hain ke phir inputs bhi barabar hone chahiye. Maan lijiye \(f(x) = \log_a x\), jahan \(a > 0\), \(a \ne 1\), \(x \in\, ]0, \infty[\). Ab \(s, t \in\, ]0, \infty[\) koi bhi do numbers lein jin ke liye
\[f(s) = f(t)\]
\[\Rightarrow \log_a s = \log_a t\]
\[\Rightarrow a^{\log_a s} = a^{\log_a t}\]
\[\Rightarrow s = t\]
Is liye logarithmic function one to one hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Har step mein kya hua? Pehla step sirf \(f\) ki jagah \(\log_a\) likhna hai. Doosre step mein dono taraf base \(a\) ki power li gayi; agar do cheezein barabar hain to un par same kaam karne se nateeja bhi barabar rehta hai. Teesre step mein identity \(a^{\log_a x} = x\) lagi (yeh topic 1.6 ki chauthi identity ki sahi shakal hai), jis ne baayen taraf \(s\) aur daayen taraf \(t\) bana diya.
Graph par is ka matlab: koi bhi horizontal line (seedhi aari lakeer) curve ko zyada se zyada ek jagah kaat-ti hai. Isay horizontal line test kehte hain.
(ii) Vertical Asymptote of Logarithmic Functions

Pehle samajh lein ke vertical asymptote kya hota hai, phir log function ke liye isay dhoondenge. Maan lijiye \(f(x) = \log_a x\), jahan \(a > 0\), \(a \ne 1\), \(x > 0\). Definition se \(x = a^{y}\). Ab hum dekhenge ke jab \(x\) right side se zero ke qareeb jaye to \(y\) ka kya banta hai. Base ki do soorton (cases) ko alag alag dekhte hain:

blocks.title: Vertical Asymptote of a Function
blocks.text:
Kitab ka box: vertical asymptote (woh khari lakeer jis ke qareeb graph jata hai magar usay chhoota nahi) ek vertical line \(x = c\) hai jis ke qareeb jate hue function \(f(x)\) be-hadd (without bound) barhta ya ghatta hai, jab \(x \to c\). Limit ki zabaan mein, \(x = c\) function \(y = f(x)\) ka vertical asymptote hai agar:
\[\lim_{x \to c^{+}} f(x) = \pm\infty\]
ya
\[\lim_{x \to c^{-}} f(x) = \pm\infty\]

Jab \(x \to 0^{+}\) (yani \(x\) positive rehte hue zero ke qareeb jata hai), to
\[\Rightarrow a^{y} \to 0^{+}\]
\[\Rightarrow y \to -\infty\]
\[\Rightarrow \log_a x \to -\infty\]
Is liye
\[\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} f(x) = -\infty\]
Kyun: base 1 se bara ho to us ki power zero ke qareeb tabhi aati hai jab power bohat bara negative number ho, jaise \(2^{-10} = \frac{1}{1024}\).

Ab bhi \(x \to 0^{+}\), to
\[\Rightarrow a^{y} \to 0^{+}\]
\[\Rightarrow y \to \infty\]
\[\Rightarrow \log_a x \to \infty\]
Is liye
\[\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} f(x) = \infty\]
Kyun: base 1 se chhota ho (jaise \(\frac{1}{2}\)) to us ki power zero ke qareeb tab aati hai jab power bohat bara positive number ho, jaise \((\frac{1}{2})^{10} = \frac{1}{1024}\).

Dono cases mein:
\[\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} f(x) = \pm\infty\]
Is liye line \(x = 0\) (yani \(y\)-axis) \(f(x) = \log_a x\) ka vertical asymptote hai. Aur kyun ke \(y = \log_a x\) har positive \(x\) par defined hai (kahin beech mein koi rukawat nahi), is liye \(x = 0\) ke ilawa koi aur asymptote nahi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Hamari misaal se dekhiye: \(\log_2 \frac{1}{1024} = -10\), jab ke \(\log_{1/2} \frac{1}{1024} = 10\). Yani \(x\) bohat chhota (zero ke qareeb) hua to log ki value bohat bari (negative ya positive) ho gayi. Curve \(y\)-axis se chipakta jata hai lekin usay kabhi chhoota nahi, kyun ke \(x = 0\) domain mein hai hi nahi.
Sirf \(x \to 0^{+}\) (right side) ki baat kyun? Kyun ke \(x < 0\) par function exist hi nahi karta, to left side se aane ka sawal hi paida nahi hota.
(iii) Logarithmic Functions are Strictly Increasing or Strictly Decreasing

Ab dekhte hain ke graph baayen se daayen chalte hue upar jata hai ya neeche. Strictly increasing ka matlab: \(x\) bara karo to \(y\) bhi zaroor bara ho. Strictly decreasing ka matlab: \(x\) bara karo to \(y\) zaroor chhota ho. Logarithmic function lijiye:
\[y(x) = f(x) = \log_a x\]
\((a > 0,\ a \ne 1,\ x > 0)\)
Maan lijiye \(x_1, x_2 \in\, ]0, \infty[\) aur \(x_1 < x_2\). Phir \(y_1 = f(x_1) = \log_a x_1\) aur \(y_2 = f(x_2) = \log_a x_2\).
Definition se: \(x_1 = a^{y_1}\) aur \(x_2 = a^{y_2}\).
Kyun ke \(x_1 < x_2\), is liye \(a^{y_1} < a^{y_2}\). Ab do cases:
Case-1:

Agar \(a > 1\) ho, to \(a^{y_1} < a^{y_2} \Rightarrow y_1 < y_2\).
Is se nateeja nikla:
\[x_1 < x_2 \Rightarrow f(x_1) < f(x_2)\]
Yani \(a > 1\) ho to \(y = \log_a x\) strictly increasing hai.
Kyun: topic 1.4 mein hum ne dekha tha ke \(a > 1\) ho to bari power bari value deti hai. To chhoti value \(a^{y_1}\) chhoti power \(y_1\) se hi aa sakti hai.
Case-2:

Agar \(0 < a < 1\) ho, to \(a^{y_1} < a^{y_2} \Rightarrow y_1 > y_2\).
Is se nateeja nikla:
\[x_1 < x_2 \Rightarrow f(x_1) > f(x_2)\]
Yani \(0 < a < 1\) ho to \(y = \log_a x\) strictly decreasing hai.
Kyun: base 1 se chhota ho to bari power chhoti value deti hai, misaal \((\frac{1}{2})^{3} = \frac{1}{8}\) jo \((\frac{1}{2})^{2} = \frac{1}{4}\) se chhota hai. Is liye chhoti value bari power se aati hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Neeche wala table dono rawaiye ek saath dikhata hai. Upar wali row (\(\log_2 x\)) mein \(x\) barhne par values barhti hain: \(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3\). Neeche wali row (\(\log_{1/2} x\)) mein wahi numbers ulte sign ke saath hain, is liye values ghatti hain. Khud sochiye: kya aap ne note kiya ke dono rows mein \(x = 1\) par value 0 hai? Yahi agla point hai.

blocks.caption: Teaching note: ek base 1 se bara aur ek 1 se chhota, values ka table (hamari taraf se, kitab mein nahi)

blocks.text: (iv) Intercepts and Continuity of Logarithmic Functions
Intercept ka matlab woh point jahan graph kisi axis ko kaat-ta hai. Logarithmic function \(y = \log_a x\) \((a > 0,\ a \ne 1,\ x > 0)\) ke liye:
Intercepts:

items:
(i) \(x\)-intercept ke liye \(y = 0\) rakhte hain (kyun ke \(x\)-axis par har point ka \(y\) zero hota hai):
\[\log_a x = 0\]
\[\Rightarrow x = a^{0} = 1\]
Is liye \(y = \log_a x\) ka graph \(x\)-axis ko point \((1, 0)\) par kaat-ta hai, base chahe jo bhi ho.
(ii) \(y\)-intercept ke liye \(x = 0\) rakhna parta, lekin \(y = \log_a x\) \(x = 0\) par defined hi nahi. Is liye koi \(y\)-intercept nahi.

blocks.text: Continuity:

Function \(y = \log_a x\) har \(x > 0\) par continuous hai. Continuous ka matlab: graph mein koi toot, chhalaang ya surakh nahi; aap pencil uthaye baghair poora curve bana sakte hain. Is ki wajah yeh hai ke
\[\lim_{x \to c} \log_a x = \log_a c\]
har \(c > 0\) ke liye, yani jis point ki taraf \(x\) jata hai, function ki value bhi wahi value ban jati hai jo us point par hai.
Is liye function apne domain mein kahin toot-ta ya chhalaang nahi lagata.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Point \((1, 0)\) har logarithmic graph ka saanjha (common) point hai, kyun ke har base ke liye \(a^{0} = 1\). Isay exponential se milaiye: har exponential graph \((0, 1)\) se guzarta hai. Yeh dono points line \(y = x\) mein ek doosre ka aaina (mirror image) hain. Khud sochiye: \(\log_7 1\) aur \(\log_{0.3} 1\) kitne hain? Dono zero.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Neeche ke sawal khud hal kijiye, phir jawab se milaiye:
1. \(y = \log_5 x\) barhta hai ya ghatta hai? (Barhta hai, kyun ke base 5 > 1.)
2. \(y = \log_{0.2} x\) mein jab \(x \to 0^{+}\) to \(y\) kahan jata hai? (\(+\infty\), kyun ke base 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan hai.)
3. \(y = \log_4 x\) ka \(x\)-intercept kya hai? (\((1, 0)\).) Aur \(y\)-intercept? (Koi nahi.)
4. Agar \(\log_3 s = \log_3 7\) ho to \(s\) kitna hai? (7, kyun ke log one-to-one hai.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\log_a x\) one-to-one hai: \(\log_a s = \log_a t \Rightarrow s = t\).
2. Vertical asymptote \(x = 0\): \(a > 1\) par \(\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} \log_a x = -\infty\), \(0 < a < 1\) par \(+\infty\). Koi aur asymptote nahi.
3. \(a > 1\): strictly increasing; \(0 < a < 1\): strictly decreasing.
4. \(x\)-intercept \((1, 0)\) har base ke liye; \(y\)-intercept nahi.
5. Har \(x > 0\) par continuous.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\log_a x\) ka asymptote \(y = 0\) likh dena. Woh \(a^{x}\) ka asymptote hai; \(\log_a x\) ka vertical asymptote \(x = 0\) hai. Yaad rakhiye: inverse mein horizontal, vertical ban jata hai.
2. \(y\)-intercept dhoondna: \(x = 0\) domain se bahar hai, is liye intercept hai hi nahi.
3. Yeh samajhna ke har log function barhta hai. Base \(0 < a < 1\) ho to function ghatta hai.
